Russian President Vladimir Putin has built and maintained his position for most of his 25 years in power by acting as the final arbiter of policy, choosing between the Federal Security Service (FSB) and other groups that favor a less repressive approach.



In recent months, as his popularity has fallen, Putin has tilted ever more frequently toward the FSB and given it ever more power over an increasingly broad range of Russian life.



While Putin still retains the ability to choose, his tilt toward the FSB is reducing his ability to act against it as its powers grow and are institutionalized, a development that likely presages more repression both during his time in office and beyond.
